angle: Without an orchestration layer, AI in CX just creates faster silos.
sourceTitle: Orchestration is the new challenge for CX in the age of AI agents
linkedinPost:
AI agents are flooding CX. The wiring behind them isn’t.

VentureBeat highlights a reality we see daily: enterprises are gluing conversational AI onto legacy systems never built for it. The result? Impressive demos, chaotic operations. Tickets bounce, context is lost, and humans inherit the mess.

My take: orchestration isn’t optional; it’s the product. You need a layer that routes, remembers, and governs across channels — voice, chat, email — and across bots and humans.

What to build or buy now:
- Policy-aware routing (who/what handles which intents under which risk rules)
- Shared memory and case lineage so context survives handoffs
- Live transfer with receipts (what the bot did, what’s pending)
- Observability tied to CX metrics: containment, CSAT, handle time, recontact rate
- Fall-forward design: graceful degradation to a human, not a dead end

If no one owns orchestration, the customer will notice — and your agents (human and AI) will burn out cleaning it up.

Who owns orchestration in your org today: CX, IT, or a dedicated platform team? #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption #AIStrategy
xPost: AI in CX without orchestration = faster silos. Route by policy, preserve context, transfer with receipts, and measure outcomes — not just intent accuracy. Make orchestration someone’s job. #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI
